# An interval that contains a ball, two-limb center

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_to_interval_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An interval with bounds of two limbs that contains the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$, each bound within $A\lvert v\rvert + B$ of the bound $v$ of the ball:

$$Z \supseteq [c - r, c + r].$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $c = c_0 + c_1$, $z_l = z_{l0} + z_{l1}$, $z_u = z_{u0} + z_{u1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Interval<T, 2>(X)` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `Interval<T, 2>` | explicit; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `X.lower()` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $z_l$; the kernel computes both bounds; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |
| `X.upper()` | `Ball<T, 2>` | `Expansion<T, 2>` | $z_u$; the kernel computes both bounds; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode; not `constexpr` |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- the ball of center $c$ and radius $r$ is a canonical ball: a finite ball (finite center, normalized, finite radius $\ge 0$), the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$), or the empty set (every limb a NaN).

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval, empty exactly when the ball $X$ of center $c$ and radius $r$ is.
- $Z$ contains $x$ for every $x \in X$: the whole line gives $[-\infty, +\infty]$.
- For a finite ball and a bounded $Z$: $z_l \le c - r$ and $c + r \le z_u$, each within $A\,\lvert v\rvert + B$ of the bound $v$ ($c \mp r$), with the constants $A$ and $B$ below.
- When $c - r = 0$, $z_l = c - r$ exactly.
- When $c + r = 0$, $z_u = c + r$ exactly.
- For a finite ball, $Z$ is bounded when every member $x$ of the ball has $\lvert x\rvert \le 2^{e_{\max}-2}$.

The constants of the bound, from `gen/claims.json`: $A$ is `(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^3)*up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u))+2*u^2)*(1+unit(add_2_2))/(1-u)` and $B$ is `2*(1+u)^2*(1/2*up((1+u)^3)*eta+up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))+eta+(2*(1+u)^3*up((1+u)^3)*up(unit(add_2_2)/(1-unit(add_2_2))*(1+u))+2*u^2)/(1-u)*tiny(add_2_2)`, where `up( )` is a constant as `T` rounds it up (the $E$, $G$, $H$ of a radius) and `unit( )`, `tiny( )` are the constants of the center's kernel; $N$ is the smallest normal number of `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| $A / u^2$ | $8.0000000000000091 \times 10^{0}$ | $8.0000048875823637 \times 10^{0}$ |
| $B / N$ | $2.0000000000000018 \times 10^{0}$ | $2.000000953674423 \times 10^{0}$ |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 3 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_to_interval_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert2.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallConvert2.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_to_interval_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_to_interval_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the directed sums of two limbs of the center and the radius (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_to_interval_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_to_interval_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`make_2`](make_2.md), [`add_down_2_2`](add_down_2_2.md), [`add_up_2_2`](add_up_2_2.md).

```
# An interval with 2-limb bounds that contains a ball with a 2-limb center (milestone2.md, "One
# enclosure interface", "Midpoint, radius and the conversions", "Ball to interval"): the directed sums
# of two limbs of the center and the radius, add_down_2_2(c, -r) and add_up_2_2(c, r), then the
# selects of interval_add_2 (a bound that the finite core does not return finite is the infinity on
# its side), and the empty set selected by the test of the radius. Each bound is within A |v| + B of
# c -+ r, the constants of the sum, and a bound c -+ r that is exactly zero is returned as zero, by
# the rule of the directed sums. The whole line gives [-inf, +inf], through the same selects. The
# radius is made a 2-limb number by make_2 (the page writes (-r, 0) and (r, 0)), so that no limb is
# added to a literal zero; its guard changes nothing of a radius, a limb of an object. These are the
# values of lower() and upper() of a Ball<T, 2>. Bounded when every member of the ball is at most
# 2^(emax-2) in magnitude, as the sum of two limbs.

nr       = neg(r)
(n0, n1) = make_2(nr)
(p0, p1) = make_2(r)
(l0, l1) = add_down_2_2(c0, c1, n0, n1)
(h0, h1) = add_up_2_2(c0, c1, p0, p1)
al       = abs(l0)
fl       = lt(al, const inf)
ah       = abs(h0)
fh       = lt(ah, const inf)
mi       = neg(const inf)
a0       = select(fl, l0, mi)
a1       = select(fl, l1, 0)
b0       = select(fh, h0, const inf)
b1       = select(fh, h1, 0)
ne       = eq(r, r)
zl0      = select(ne, a0, const inf)
zl1      = select(ne, a1, 0)
zu0      = select(ne, b0, mi)
zu1      = select(ne, b1, 0)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_to_interval_2)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 904 806 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
